result:
task: Add red-first acceptance tests for DEC-747's sessions boundary (P-1) to W2-20's suite, and correct the "four recorded commands" counts in the W1-07 and W1-26 READMEs
status: DONE. Commit `d82619c3` is in place; the two cases the decision makes stricter fail, as the README says they should, and the other 23 cases pass.
work_completed: Added one parametrised test with 3 cases, `test_DEC_747_at_most_8_holds_after_the_start`, in `test_w2_20_gate.py`. It builds a weighted count of 7 (3 heavy + 1 light) or 8 (3 heavy + 2 light) from live child processes, uses DEC-742's default maximum of 8 with no `gate.json`, and checks: [7, a light start opens], [7, a heavy start is refused] and [8, the reading shuts and a light start is refused]. The heavy start is asked with `gov resources --check --heavy`, the same flag `--register` already uses; a start check with no `--heavy` is a light start. `Machine.check()` in the support gained a `heavy=` keyword, and the support comment now calls the defaults DEC-742's. No existing test was revised, because none contradicts the decision: each one uses counts clearly inside or over the limit (2 of 3, 3 of 1, 4 of 3, 9 of 8, 0 or 1 against a maximum of 1 or 8). In the W2-20 README I updated: the run-2 note, the start-check row of the interface table, the paragraph on the heavy start, the gate's sessions condition with each reason's `reading` and `threshold`, the configuration defaults (now DEC-742's), red run 2, the KPI table (success 2 and the failure line), the count (25 cases, 18 functions), and P-1 marked as decided by DEC-747 (delegated, staged).
files_changed: tests/acceptance/W2-20/test_w2_20_gate.py; tests/acceptance/W2-20/w2_20_support.py; tests/acceptance/W2-20/README.md; tests/acceptance/W1-07/README.md; tests/acceptance/W1-26/README.md
evidence: `git log --oneline -2` shows `d82619c3 W2-20 (DAEO-r30l): the sessions boundary of the start check (DEC-747)` above `2ceae1e9 Merge w2/integrate into w2/W2-20: …`. Trailers: Task: DAEO-r30l / Role: independent-test-designer / Implements: DEC-729 / Implements: DEC-742 / Rewrite-Reason: DEC-747 (delegated) settles P-1, the sessions boundary: one new parametrised test, --heavy on the start check in the support, no existing test revised; README counts in W1-07 and W1-26 follow 173e8e97 (resources recorded beside DEC-542's four) / Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5. `git status --short` after the commit printed nothing. The hooks folder holds only `*.sample` files. `gov.__file__` line: `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-20/src/gov/__init__.py`
tests: `tests/acceptance/W2-20` (run in full, no `-x`): **2 failed, 23 passed** (25 cases). Red reasons as I saw them: (1) `[7, a heavy start is refused]`: `the refusal is not the named error RESOURCE_GATE_SHUT: {'code': 'RESOURCE_REGISTER_INVALID', 'message': '--ticket, --session-role and --heavy go with --register', 'details': {}}`, so the start check does not take the new session's weight. (2) `[8, the reading shuts and a light start is refused]`: `8 of 8 leaves no room and must read shut: {...}` / `assert True is False`; the reading counts 8 as within the maximum rather than below it, and the case stops before its light start check. `[7, a light start opens]` passes. I also ran W1-07 `test_w1_07_recorded_commands.py` (6 passed) and W1-26 `test_w1_26_recorded_commands.py` (10 passed, 2 failed: the two `resources` cases).
discoveries: (1) At this commit, W1-26's two `resources` cases are red: `test_a_recorded_command_without_its_module_is_a_finding_that_names_it[resources]` (no finding names `resources`) and `test_a_skill_may_name_a_recorded_gov_command[resources]` (`unknown gov command 'resources'`). The first belongs to the engineer's `src/gov/check/commands.py` line (DEC-747 P-A). I can't tell whether the skill validator reads that same list or a list in a file outside W2-20's paths, because I may not read `src/`. (2) Two W1-07 README lines (208 and 214) still name the three recorded gov commands and "fifteen commands" without `resources`. They don't say "four", so I left them as the brief asks.
risks: The start check's `sessions` reason uses the count after the start as its `reading` (for example `(9, 8)`), while the reading's reason uses the live count (`(8, 8)`). This is stated in the README and held by the test, but it is a choice of mine: the decision fixes the comparison, not the reason's numbers. A heavy start that fits exactly (6 + 2 = 8) has no case of its own; that follows STANDARD, with no combinatorial expansion.
lessons: To keep the references in the test docstrings valid, the section titles in the W1-07 and W1-26 READMEs keep their old start ("The four commands of DEC-542", "The four recorded commands in the checks") and add "and W2-20's `resources` … five recorded". In the "Today" columns, the status when each row was written is kept, and the status at `2ceae1e9` is added next to it.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: Whether the skill validator's list is within reach of W2-20's paths (see discoveries); the engineer or lead should check when making the W1-26 `resources` cases green.
recommended_next_action: The engineer adds `--heavy` to `--check`, makes the start check count the new session's weight and the reading shut at the maximum, and records `resources` in `src/gov/check/commands.py`; then the lead re-runs W2-20, W1-07 and W1-26 under this worktree's `PYTHONPATH`.

README lines corrected:
- **W1-07:** the section title (line 203); the case-table rows for `test_the_recorded_commands_are_four_…` (now "exactly five … DEC-542's four and `resources`, recorded by W2-20 in DEC-542's form (`173e8e97`)") and `test_a_recorded_gov_command_is_offered_…` ("4: … and W2-20's `resources`", "green, all four"); the count line ("6 cases (5 before W2-20's `resources`), all green at `2ceae1e9`").
- **W1-26:** the section title ("12 cases", five recorded); the `core-commands` bullet ("each of the five"); the rows for `…without_its_module…` (5 cases), `…every_module_present…` ("the twelve and the five") and `…may_name_a_recorded_gov_command` (4 cases), each with its status when written and at `2ceae1e9`; the tally line ("7 red, 3 green when written with the four; at `2ceae1e9`, with `resources`: 2 red (its two cases), 10 green").
